subject: FinTechCo - Follow-up: pricing + US vs EU residency impact
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@fintechco.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up + quick pricing notes (US vs EU residency)

Hi Alex — thanks again for the time today. Recap and next steps from our discovery:

Summary of your intake:
- Monthly token volume range: 1M–5M tokens (you mentioned a likely steady-state around 3–4M).
- Primary workload: customer-facing generative responses + account summary embeddings (latency-sensitive).
- Data residency ask: EU-hosted instances for EU customer data / logs; US for rest.
- Target procurement: decision window ~May; pilot request next 2–3 weeks.

Quick pricing / unit-economics notes (high level, ballpark):
- Hosted (US region): ~$300 per 1M tokens (assumes mixed prompt+completion tokens, typical batching).
- Hosted (EU region): ~15% uplift vs US -> ~$345 per 1M (higher infra and networking costs, regional capacity premium).
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): from ~$220 per 1M (12‑month commit + infra fee) — best for predictable 4M+ volumes.
- Data residency premium: expect an additional uplift for strict residency + KMS/HSM usage and increased storage/retention controls; ballpark 10–20% depending on retention and audit requirements.
- Effective unit economics: with batching, KV caching, and prefix reuse we typically see 10–25% lower effective $/1M vs raw hosted price.

Budget range we discussed: ~$5k–$20k/month depending on pilot scale. If your finance target is a ballpark $/1M target, you mentioned wanting something in the mid-$200s to low-$300s per 1M as a target — we can aim to get close to that in the US hosted or with a committed Dedicated plan.

Next steps / asks:
1) Can you confirm expected steady-state monthly tokens (best guess is fine) and whether EU residency is required for all EU customer data or just specific subsets?
2) Do you have a preferred procurement timeline / procurement owner (we can prepare a standard SOW + pricing appendix)?
3) We attached a short pricing sheet with committed tiers and residency notes — can you confirm receipt and whether you want a dedicated vs hosted line-item breakout?

I’ve attached the pricing sheet and a short figure that sketches the residency uplift. Happy to jump on a 30-min follow-up to align on pilot scope and timelines.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0123
redwoodinference.com

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 09:08:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Follow-up + quick pricing notes (US vs EU residency)

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. Confirmations and a few clarifying Qs:

- Our estimate: steady-state 3–4M tokens/month after pilot. Pilot month will be around 500–800k.
- Budget: target ~$12k–$18k/month for production (we can stretch during pilot).
- Residency: yes, EU residency required for EU customer data and logs for regulatory reasons (GDPR + internal compliance). We’d like EU data to never leave EU-controlled hosts.
- Ask: can you provide a line-item breakout showing hosted US vs hosted EU vs dedicated committed price per 1M tokens (and any additional per-month infra or orchestration fees)? Also include any one-time onboarding or migration fees if applicable.

Also looping procurement: I’m the product lead; procurement/legal will want an SOW and SOC2 evidence before signing. Can you share the SOC2 report link and a sample SOW?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — happy to take a follow-up call next week.

— Alex
Alex Rivera
Head of Product, Integrations | FinTechCo
alex.rivera@fintechco.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@fintechco.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up + quick pricing notes (US vs EU residency)

Alex — great, thanks for the clarity. Attached is a concise breakout and a draft SOW link. Key items below (line-item view):

Line-item pricing (ballpark, list prices before discounts):
- Hosted (US): $300 per 1M tokens
- Hosted (EU): $345 per 1M tokens (15% regional uplift)
- Dedicated Reserved (12mo commit): $220 per 1M tokens + $1,500/mo per cluster orchestration fee (example pricing for a medium pool)
- Onboarding / one-time: $4,000 (technical onboarding, secure keying, private networking) — negotiable for committed deals
- Data residency add-ons: KMS + HSM setup, additional retention/audit logs: typical uplift 5–10% on top of region price; strict egress controls and isolated infra can add another fixed infra premium.

Notes on assumptions and unit economics:
- Prices above assume token mix and batching patterns similar to what we discussed. If you have very short prompts and small completions throughput/latency becomes the driver and unit cost can be higher.
- With batching and KV/prefix caching, teams at your volume typically see a 10–20% effective reduction vs list hosted prices.
- Committed Dedicated pricing assumes a 12-month minimum and standard support SLA; we can share an exact committed quote if you confirm expected monthly tokens.

Security / compliance links included in the Drive folder (SOC 2 Type II and encryption architecture). I’ve also added a sample SOW and a checklist for EU residency (controls we enforce, encryption, in-region logging, and legal attachments).

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm steady-state estimate (3–4M) and pilot target (500–800k).
- We prepare a draft committed quote + SOW for your procurement to review (I can add a dedicated line-item table for hosted vs dedicated per your ask).
- Pilot kickoff week of May 10 — technical onboarding and sample traffic.

If that works I’ll get a formal quote out by EOD Tuesday.

Best,
Marissa
